bib.title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235

question: Can LLM pre-training and fine-tuning be made memory-efficient while still learning full parameters, by projecting gradients (not weights) into a low-rank subspace?
hypothesis: Weight gradients become low-rank during training, so optimizer states kept for a low-rank projection of the gradient, with periodically switched subspaces, match full-rank training at far lower memory than LoRA-style reparameterisation.
contributions: GaLore: gradient low-rank projection allowing full-parameter learning with optimizer states in a compact space
Theory: gradient becomes low-rank for reversible networks; convergence with fixed projections
Pre-training LLaMA up to 7B (19.7B tokens) and GLUE fine-tuning; 8-bit GaLore trains 7B within 24GB

method.summary: Per weight matrix, GaLore projects the gradient with the top-r singular vectors of the gradient (refreshed every T steps), runs Adam/AdamW/8-bit Adam/Adafactor in the compact space, projects the update back and adds it to the full weights. Evaluated on C4 LLaMA pre-training (60M to 7B) against Full-Rank, Low-Rank, LoRA, ReLoRA, and on RoBERTa-Base GLUE fine-tuning, with memory and throughput measurement.
method.task: LLM pre-training (next-token, C4) and fine-tuning (GLUE, SQuAD, OpenAssistant, Belle-1M)

datasets.name: C4
datasets.size: 1.3B / 2.6B / 7.8B / 13.1B / 19.7B tokens for 60M/130M/350M/1B/7B (Table 5); Table 2 text lists 1.1B/2.2B/6.4B/13.1B for 60M-1B
datasets.source: Raffel et al. 2020 cleaned Common Crawl

datasets.name: GLUE
datasets.split: 8 tasks: CoLA STS-B MRPC RTE SST2 MNLI QNLI QQP

training.optimizer: Adam (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-8) with GaLore; also AdamW, 8-bit Adam, Adafactor with first-order stats
training.lr: GaLore 0.01 with scale alpha 0.25 (effective 0.0025) for all pre-training sizes; baselines tuned from {0.01,0.005,0.001,0.0005,0.0001}
training.lr_schedule: cosine annealing, decaying to 10% of initial lr
training.batch_size: 131K tokens (pre-training); 16 (32 for CoLA) for GLUE; token batch 256 for memory measurement
training.hardware: NVIDIA A100 GPUs; 7B run on 8 nodes, 64 A100 GPUs
training.seeds: single trial for 7B; seeds otherwise not stated

other.glue_lr_r4: 1e-5 (MNLI SST-2 QNLI QQP RTE STS-B), 3e-5 (MRPC CoLA)
other.glue_lr_r8: 1e-5 MNLI QNLI CoLA, 2e-5 SST-2 MRPC QQP RTE, 3e-5 STS-B
other.projection: one projector only (P if m<=n else Q), from SVD of current gradient
other.layers_applied: all multi-head attention and feed-forward layers
other.T_range_note: T between 50 and 1000 makes no much difference

limits: Authors list open problems: vision transformers and diffusion models untested, low-memory projection matrices (quantisation) left for future work, elastic data-distributed training on low-bandwidth consumer hardware unexplored.
7B comparison is a single trial with no hyperparameter tuning against 8-bit Adam; only perplexity at 19.7B tokens, no downstream evaluation of the pre-trained 7B.
Current GaLore implementation has 17% throughput overhead vs 8-bit Adam; SVD cost claimed <10% but not measured separately.
Theory covers reversible networks (not self-attention) and fixed projections; Transformers handled only for FFN project-up weight under JoMA assumptions.
24GB feasibility relies on per-layer weight updates, small per-GPU token batch (up to 500, 4096 with activation checkpointing); no end-to-end 7B training on a 4090 reported.
Fine-tuning gains over LoRA are small (85.89 vs 85.61 GLUE average) and below full fine-tuning (86.28).

terms.definition: Gradient low-rank projection: update rule W_T = W0 + eta sum P_t rho_t(P_t^T G_t Q_t) Q_t^T, with P, Q projection matrices

code.snippet:
for weight in model.parameters():
  grad = weight.grad
  lor_grad = project(grad)
  lor_update = update(lor_grad)
  update = project_back(lor_update)
  weight.data += update
